point: Claiming before full retirement age (67 for anyone born in 1960 or later) permanently reduces the benefit; 40 years of work only makes her eligible and does not remove the reduction.
Working while claiming before full retirement age triggers the retirement earnings test, so she will not get the full benefit on top of her paycheck.

Reduction: she is first 62 for a whole month in April 2027 (born March 18), so benefits start April 2027, 59 months early: a 29.58% reduction, about $1,690 a month instead of $2,400 (roughly 30% and $1,680 is an acceptable approximation).

2027 earnings test: limit $25,560 (announced by SSA October 14, 2026); $1 withheld for every $2 over the limit; all 2027 earnings count, including January to March; with $38,000 the excess is $12,440 and the withholding is $6,220 for the year.

SSA withholds whole monthly checks: about four months (April to July benefits), with the small excess repaid later, so almost no Social Security arrives until about September 2027; the first-year monthly rule does not help because about $3,167 a month in wages is above the 2027 monthly limit of $2,130.
Withheld months are not lost: the benefit is recalculated upward at full retirement age.

A 2027 monthly budget showing the paycheck (about $3,167 a month gross) every month, little or no Social Security for the first months, then about $1,690 a month; and noting that up to 85% of her benefits may be taxable at her income.
Suggests she check her own figures with SSA's calculators or her my Social Security account.
